marrow__ANAT_CH62_Q015.takeaway: Spinal sensory ganglia contain pseudounipolar neurons; bipolar neurons occur in special sensory pathways.
marrow__ANAT_CH62_Q015.displayText:
Spinal sensory ganglia contain pseudounipolar neurons; bipolar neurons occur in special sensory pathways.

Bipolar neurons are not seen in spinal ganglia; spinal ganglia contain pseudounipolar neurons.

Examples listed: unipolar neurons in mesencephalic nucleus, pseudounipolar neurons in sensory/spinal ganglia, bipolar neurons in spiral and vestibular ganglia and retina, and multipolar neurons in cerebrum and cerebellum.
emphasis: Spinal sensory ganglia contain pseudounipolar neurons; bipolar neurons occur in special sensory pathways

rationales.a: Spiral ganglia contain bipolar neurons associated with hearing.
rationales.c: Vestibular ganglia contain bipolar primary sensory neurons.
rationales.d: Retinal bipolar cells are named bipolar neurons and relay visual signals.

marrow__ANAT_CH62_Q016.takeaway: A reflex arc contains a receptor, afferent neuron, integration, efferent neuron and effector; “affector” is not a component.
marrow__ANAT_CH62_Q016.displayText:
A reflex arc contains a receptor, afferent neuron, integration, efferent neuron and effector; “affector” is not a component.

A reflex arc contains an effector, usually a muscle, not an affector.

A monosynaptic reflex arc consists of receptor, sensory/afferent neuron, motor/efferent neuron and effector.
emphasis: A reflex arc contains a receptor, afferent neuron, integration, efferent neuron and effector; “affector” is not a component

rationales.a: The receptor detects the stimulus and initiates the reflex arc.
rationales.b: A sensory neuron carries afferent input toward the CNS.
rationales.c: A motor neuron carries efferent output to the effector.

marrow__ANAT_CH62_Q017.takeaway: Microglia are mesoderm/monocyte-lineage immune cells; the other listed macroglia arise from neuroectoderm.
marrow__ANAT_CH62_Q017.displayText:
Microglia are mesoderm/monocyte-lineage immune cells; the other listed macroglia arise from neuroectoderm.

Microglial cells are not neuroectodermal; they are mesoderm-derived, possibly from circulating monocytes entering the CNS during fetal/early postnatal life.

Macroglia of neuroectodermal origin include astrocytes, oligodendrocytes and glioblasts.
emphasis: Microglia are mesoderm/monocyte-lineage immune cells; the other listed macroglia arise from neuroectoderm

rationales.a: Astrocytes derive from neuroectoderm and support CNS neurons.
rationales.b: Oligodendrocytes derive from neuroectoderm and myelinate CNS axons.
rationales.d: Glioblasts are neuroectodermal precursors of CNS macroglia, not microglia.

marrow__ANAT_CH62_Q018.takeaway: The blood–brain barrier requires nonfenestrated endothelial cells joined by tight junctions, with basement membrane and astrocytic end-feet support.
marrow__ANAT_CH62_Q018.displayText:
The blood–brain barrier requires nonfenestrated endothelial cells joined by tight junctions, with basement membrane and astrocytic end-feet support.

Fenestrated capillary endothelium is not part of the blood-brain barrier.

The blood-brain barrier consists of capillary endothelium with tight junctions and no fenestrations, endothelial basement membrane, and astrocyte end-feet covering capillary walls. It permits selective passage of blood constituents into nervous tissue.
emphasis: The blood–brain barrier requires nonfenestrated endothelial cells joined by tight junctions, with basement membrane and astrocytic end-feet support

rationales.a: Tight-junctioned nonfenestrated capillary endothelium is a core BBB component.
rationales.b: The endothelial basement membrane contributes to the BBB structure.
rationales.c: Astrocyte end-feet support and help maintain the barrier.

marrow__ANAT_CH62_Q019.takeaway: Peripheral nerve plexuses are formed by ventral rami; dorsal rami continue segmentally to intrinsic back muscles and skin.
marrow__ANAT_CH62_Q019.displayText:
Peripheral nerve plexuses are formed by ventral rami; dorsal rami continue segmentally to intrinsic back muscles and skin.

Nerve plexuses are formed only by ventral rami.

The spinal nerve exits the intervertebral foramen and divides into ventral and dorsal rami. Cervical, brachial, lumbar, sacral and coccygeal plexuses are formed from ventral rami, not dorsal rami.
emphasis: Peripheral nerve plexuses are formed by ventral rami; dorsal rami continue segmentally to intrinsic back muscles and skin

rationales.a: Dorsal rami remain segmental and do not form the major cervical, brachial or lumbosacral plexuses.
rationales.c: Dorsal roots carry sensory fibers into the cord; plexuses are formed from peripheral ventral rami.
rationales.d: Ventral roots carry motor axons and join dorsal roots to make spinal nerves; plexuses form from ventral rami after that union.

marrow__ANAT_CH62_Q020.takeaway: Sympathetic activation increases sweating, blood pressure and pupil diameter; dry skin would not be expected.
marrow__ANAT_CH62_Q020.displayText:
Sympathetic activation increases sweating, blood pressure and pupil diameter; dry skin would not be expected.

Dry skin is not expected with sympathetic stimulation.

The sympathetic nervous system arises from the lateral horn of T1-L2 spinal segments (thoracolumbar outflow). Sympathetic effects listed include sweating (sudomotor), arrector-pili contraction (pilomotor), raised blood pressure (vasomotor), dilated pupils, dry mouth and tachycardia.

Examples of sympathomimetic drugs listed are phenylephrine, albuterol, cocaine and amphetamines.
emphasis: Sympathetic activation increases sweating, blood pressure and pupil diameter; dry skin would not be expected

rationales.a: Increased sympathetic vascular and cardiac activity can raise blood pressure.
rationales.b: Sympathetic sudomotor activity increases sweat secretion.
rationales.c: Sympathetic activation contracts the radial iris muscle and dilates the pupils.
